newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper seen flirting with $2,400 again.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper seen flirting with $2,400 again.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper is likely to rechallenge the psychological $2,400 resistance further on Monday as charts head for a bullish cross and short-term spreads widen, analysts and traders said.
The prospect of another strike in Chile will also buoy the market.
Aluminium is still consolidating, but an encouraging close above $1,600 on Friday may give it a boost towards $1,625.
COPPER - Ballooning spreads and strengthening technical charts would help the metal to overcome the important $2,400 resistance, analysts said.

"The close (on Friday) is underpinned by the upwardly trending technical indicators, which is suggestive of further challenges of resistance at $2,400," said Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff in a report.
Other analysts said a bullish crossing of the 10- and 30-day moving averages, now on the cards, would further strengthen the chart picture and help copper trend upwards.
The prospect of a second strike in Chile's copper sector, this time at the Quebrada Blanca mine, might also fuel the market.
Miners at Quebrada Blanca have voted overwhelmingly to reject the company's final pay offer and to strike on Wednesday. The mine produces 75,000 tonnes of copper cathodes a year.
It follows the continuing strike at the Escondida pit, where a small group of workers walked out a week ago.

Attention in copper will, however, mostly focus on the very nearby spreads such as cash/day. Traders said this could be expected to widen further from Friday's $2 towards the LME's one percent limit. The cash to threes backwardation jumped to $210 last week, up $30 on the week.
On the downside, key suppport was pegged at $2,360 which, if broken, might send the market down to $2,350, analysts said.
At 0730 GMT three months copper was quoted at $2,392 per tonne, compared with $2,384/88 at Friday's late close.
ALUMINIUM - The market finished Friday's dealings on a positive note above $1,600 and further gains were likely with resistance still intact at $1,625, traders said.

"The technical indicators are extending higher in confirmation, as we expect further strength to be shown, having now closed above the downtrend line at $1,612," said Martin Squires of brokers Rudolf Wolff.
"Dips should be viewed as buying opportunities with stops below $1,580/90," he said.
If $1,625 was breached convincingly, a rally to $1,642 might be seen. But the market was still in a consolidating phase and small retreats were also likely.
At 0730 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,630 per tonne, compared with Friday's close of $1,618/20.
-- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
